acceptance: A missing or partial final report is INCOMPLETE: never success, never acceptance and never proof of cessation. No startup success and no producer exit substitutes for final-result acceptance. An unavailable report retracts nothing already recorded, and neither one unreadable artifact nor one malformed link invalidates the others.
directory_entries_note: the whole listing, for your information. It is NEVER used to infer any artifact's state: each artifact above is classified only from files matching its own anchored name pattern.
owner: the external operator and the independent reviewer. The worker inside the run cannot observe any of these artifacts; its own report covers what it saw before termination plus the retained candidate checkpoint -- see TASK.md item 6.

publication_timeout.note: NOT ESTABLISHED, and for this vehicle NOT ESTABLISHABLE from absence. No correlated fault naming a publication step is on disk -- which is the EXPECTED state even when a publication really did time out, because the producers do not persist those faults (producer_persistence). So this says nothing either way. An absent or inaccessible report is likewise not evidence of a timeout: a run that never started, an import or startup failure (see FAILURE.md), process death, a failed read and non-timeout publication errors all leave no final report.
publication_timeout.producer_persistence: THIS VEHICLE PERSISTS NO PUBLICATION FAULT RELIABLY. Shutdown.call writes the snapshot with the faults from EARLIER calls (authoring_shutdown.py:76-81), then runs the step (:83) and appends its fault to memory only (:85), so a fault reaches disk only if a LATER Shutdown.call writes successfully. The controller final publication (authoring_enforcement.py:493) is the LAST such call, so its fault is never written; the outer publication (:588) is not a Shutdown.call and its handler at :592-595 records nothing; and a later write re-enters bounded() against the same exhausted deadline and will likely raise before writing. An exhausted deadline can also raise at :74 before the snapshot is written at all, so even the step name can be missing. ABSENCE OF A PUBLICATION FAULT IS EXPECTED AND MEANS NOTHING. Any verdict below rests on a fault FOUND ON DISK and is parsing, never proof that the producer records such faults.
publication_timeout.rule: A publication fault is reported only when a correlated artifact literally carries a TimeoutError naming one of outer outcome publication, final enforcement publication, workload publication, workload-publication. That is PARSING. Absence proves nothing, because the producers do not reliably record such faults.
